annotations.text:
Block Canvas - a shell for wiring blocks into runnable graphs.

Left: the library, categorised by what a block does. Centre: an infinite node canvas. Right: an inspector that reshapes itself around whatever is selected.

Top row is the same shell at three moments: nothing built, mid-wire, mid-run.
The right panel is the whole idea: five different selections, five different panels, one 328px column.
Every block declares typed ports. A wire is coloured by its data type, and the type is what makes a connection legal or refuses it mid-drag. Now ten types, nine categories.
One block, labelled, plus every run state - and the direct-or-bundled rule for tools.

Continuous running.

A graph with a source block (Senses: watch folder, webhook, schedule, webcam...) never finishes - it stays armed and every event runs downstream. The transport chip switches from Run to live, and the inspector with nothing selected becomes the run-mode panel.

A Loop is a dashed frame on the canvas: blocks inside repeat once per item.

The home assistant, as one graph. Left to right: senses feed specialist models, which feed an orchestrator LLM; memory stores bundle through a Memory hub the same way tools bundle through a Toolbox; the model's text goes to a display and a speaker, its thoughts to a terminal, and its actions to motors - via a tool call that waits for approval.

The library is collapsed to a rail here to make room.
Click any block to watch the inspector swap. Press Run to put the graph in flight - wires animate, status dots turn green, the console reports.
